title: A skyscraper, twelve days early
summary: The world's tallest building went from first steel to open doors in thirteen months, and finished ahead of plan.

kinds.label: Ground
kinds.detail: Clearing the site and digging down to rock.

kinds.label: Paper
kinds.detail: Contracts that had to be signed before anything could rise.

kinds.label: Steel
kinds.detail: The frame, at four and a half floors a week.

kinds.label: Finishing
kinds.detail: Everything after the frame: mast, interiors, opening day.

tasks.label: Start tearing down the hotel
tasks.detail:
The old Waldorf-Astoria stood on the site.
It closed in May 1929.

tasks.label: Dig the foundations
tasks.detail: Two shifts of 300 men dig 55 feet down, around the clock.

risks.label: The hotel is still coming down
risks.detail: Digging began before the old hotel had been completely demolished.

tasks.label: Raise the steel frame
tasks.detail:
Half the frame is up by 27 July.
It tops out twelve days ahead of schedule.

risks.label: Five workers died
risks.detail: The official count for the whole build. Newspapers of the day reported more.

tasks.label: Steel reaches floor 26
tasks.detail: Eleven weeks after the first column went in.

tasks.label: Top out the mooring mast
tasks.detail: Work on the mast starts once the steel tops out.

tasks.label: Finish the building
tasks.detail: Complete twelve days ahead of schedule, 410 days after construction began.

tasks.label: Open the doors
tasks.detail: Forty-five days ahead of the planned opening.

risks.label: Nobody to rent it
risks.detail:
Only 23 percent of the space was let in the first year.
New Yorkers called it the Empty State Building.

footnote: Under budget, too. Please do not show this page to your project manager.
